pros: Captures both quantity and quality of connections
Recursive definition captures global network structure
Strong theoretical foundation in linear algebra
Naturally identifies influential nodes in social networks
Power iteration avoids expensive full eigendecomposition
Produces smooth distribution of scores for nuanced ranking
Related to PageRank which transformed web search
Identifies hub regions in network community structure
Well-suited for undirected collaboration and friendship networks
cons: Can produce zero scores for isolated or peripheral nodes
Convergence is slow when spectral gap is small
Oscillates on bipartite graphs without modification
Does not work well for directed graphs (use PageRank or HITS)
Requires normalization at each iteration step
Results depend on graph connectivity and component structure
Power iteration requires O(V²) operations per dense iteration
Less intuitive to interpret than simpler measures
Sensitive to changes in graph structure (eigenvector perturbation)
Cannot handle graphs with multiple connected components well
Initial vector choice can affect convergence for some graphs
